request_context: Very High, 3840x2160, Windows RTX 4090 mobile. The available measurement host is Linux with RTX 3090 Ti; no target-hardware FPS claim.

environment.run_isolation: Separate XDG data/config/cache per run; same shipping custom Godot 4.7 executable and native libraries. Timed final comparisons run sequentially without overlapping builds or tests. GPU clocks were not locked.

changes.change: Seed the renderer CPU instance cache before the first packed MultiMesh upload. LOD mesh swaps can then rebuild bounds without a GPU buffer readback.
changes.cost: 80 bytes retained per tuft, within the existing bounded active chunk set. Scalar fallback already used a cache.

changes.change: Retain immutable positions, UV2 material ownership and triangle indices on the authored water mesh. WaterSurface reuses them; replaced/custom meshes retain the previous fallback.
changes.cost: 1,559,124 retained bytes on original zone1; references are shared by query caches and released with the map.

changes.change: Build occlusion faces from the existing retained figure geometry. Preserve Godot TriangleMesh vertex snapping at 0.0001 m and the existing fallback for custom meshes.
Reuse immutable habitat records in the overlapping 7x7 camera-cell window; invalidate on field/scenery/water changes. Preserve record order, seeds, locations and kinds.
changes.cost: At most 49 cells with four source lanes each. Horizontal movement queries 28 lanes instead of rebuilding the whole window; diagonal movement queries 52.

changes.change: Warm the real mesh formats and materials for every possible regional animal during zone loading. Tinted snow mice and frogs no longer introduce their shader source for the first time during camera travel.
changes.diagnosis: The only new shader/vertex-format combination in the Ingos hitch snapshot was the snow mouse tint. Callback profiling showed no corresponding multi-second script callback. An additional unchanged 1.5.0 control still stalled 3.796 seconds after the candidate run.

quality: Presets, shaders used for visible rendering, shadow quality, reflection resolution, density and draw distances are unchanged. No player-visible text or settings added.

method.held: tools/benchmarks/map_pan.gd v2: held world/session physics; live rendering/effects/UI; both camera and rig follow a wall-clock route. Does not execute camera input/smoothing/fading.
method.live: tools/benchmarks/map_pan_live.gd v1: normal world/session physics and camera controller, driven with synthetic bound keys. Includes smoothing, terrain clearance and fading. Records camera travel and simulated seconds. Not deterministic combat replay or physical input latency.
method.windows: 10 seconds per phase, 18-second warmup, stationary then first traversal then repeated traversal; each phase preceded by reset/settle.
method.timing: Wall-frame intervals are the pacing metric. GPU/readback getters and screenshots occur only at boundaries. process_ms and physics_ms are sampled engine peak monitors, not per-frame callback execution costs. Profiling and feature ablations are diagnostic only.

limits: Measurements are Linux/RTX 3090 Ti, not Windows/D3D12 or the requested laptop GPU.
Short camera sweeps on two maps are not a whole-campaign or co-op combat benchmark.

First-use pipeline/streaming spikes are reduced, not universally eliminated: the final live Gipat first traversal still had a 55.16 ms frame, and the final Ingos sweep had occasional approximately 31 ms frames.
Ingos steady repeated-traversal FPS was essentially unchanged; the material improvement there is removal of the multi-second first encounter hitch.
An early grass-only candidate run (rig-cache-b) had unexplained worse pacing; subsequent repetitions did not reproduce it. Retained as diagnostic evidence, not silently discarded.
historical_comparison_note: 1.0.4 remained around 58 FPS in the held rig sweep and still had repeated approximately 31 ms frames. Experimental.5 used Natural reflections where later Very High uses Mirror, so its approximately 65 FPS camera-only result is not a matched-quality comparison. Other v1 camera-only diagnostics are not combined with v2/live results.

failed_diagnostics.reason: Prototype omitted the engine triangle-cache snapping grid; exact geometry regression caught it. Fixed and all 3235 checks passed in camera-faces-exact.
Aborted before measurement while ensuring serialized benchmark execution; not used for results.
GPU profiler exceeded its default timestamp limit; excluded from quantitative GPU conclusions. Later profiling used a diagnostic-only 1024-query limit.

gpu_cost_diagnostic.note: Diagnostic profiler samples across the run, not pass timings for a specific camera pose. Renderer opaque/depth work dominates steady GPU time. Mirror-vs-Natural ablation is a quality comparison, not a shipped optimization.
